children: South Korea’s economy was confirmed to have grown by 0.6% QoQ in the second quarter of 2026, matching preliminary estimates but easing from 1.8% growth in the first quarter, which was the strongest quarterly expansion since Q1 2021.

GDP growth was mainly driven by robust exports, which offset downward pressure from the lingering conflict in the Middle East. Exports rose 1.3%, boosted by IT products such as semiconductors and machinery and equipment, while imports increased at a softer rate of 0.7%.
Private consumption climbed 0.4%, supported by higher spending on both goods and services, while government consumption edged up 0.1%.
Investment in intellectual property products grew by 3.4%, while facility investment advanced 0.2%.
By contrast, construction investment inched down 0.1% as civil engineering activity declined.
On a yearly basis, the economy advanced 3.7% in Q2, easing from an upwardly revised 3.8% in Q1, which marked the fastest annual growth since Q4 2021.

title: South Korea Q2 GDP Growth Confirmed at 0.6%
